author: Ocean World project, authored with Codex
geometry: Original continuous closed radial bodies, closed shaped fins, low skin tubercles, recessed small eyes and authored vertex pigmentation. No external animal geometry, photograph, texture or animation was copied.
redistribution: This new project-authored content has no additional third-party asset restrictions. It can accompany redistribution of the project. The scientific reference pages are cited only; their photos and illustrations are not bundled.

models.name: 座头鲸
models.measurement: Head-to-tail total length; longitudinal geometry spans exactly 1.0 before metre scaling.
models.authenticity: Authored visual representative; not a scan, measured individual, calibrated anatomy or natural population simulation.
models.largeShapeReferences: Mostly dark dorsal body, pale variable underside, long pectoral fins, small posterior dorsal hump, broad horizontal flukes, head tubercles and paired blowholes.
models.choreography: 0–16 seconds rising, 16–22 near the surface, 17.5–20.5 seconds short authored breath mist, 22–35 seconds descending. The timing, speed, trajectory and grouping are educational display choices.

models.name: 宽吻海豚
models.measurement: Head-to-tail total length; longitudinal geometry spans exactly 1.0 before metre scaling.
models.authenticity: Authored visual representative; not a scan, measured individual, calibrated anatomy or natural population simulation.
models.largeShapeReferences: Gray dorsal body, pale underside, continuous short blunt beak with forehead, swept dorsal fin, paired pectoral fins, horizontal flukes and one blowhole.
models.choreography: Six independently phased animals travel in the same broad direction with staggered depth and lateral separation. This is a representative authored pod, not evidence of a naturally associated whale-and-dolphin group.

limits: The whale and dolphin shapes are original visual representatives and retain an authored model appearance; no scan fidelity is claimed.
Vertical fluke/fin movement, surface waves, suspended particles and breath mist are display effects rather than anatomy, fluid or respiratory simulations.
One whale and six dolphins are shown as separate representative Caribbean observations in one authored open-water composition; natural interspecies association is not claimed.
The pelagic chapter has no seabed because the bottom is outside this near-surface observation volume, not because all open ocean has identical depth.
This independent scene does not load, rewrite, advance or save the existing persistent ecology.
